overview: Health Topics Countries Newsroom Emergencies Data About WHO Bacterial vaginosis (BV) is a very common cause of vaginal discharge among women of reproductive age. BV prevalence varies across countries and population groups, but a recent systematic review and meta-analysis of the global BV prevalence among women of reproductive age range from 23–29%.
symptoms: a strong fishy or musty odour from the vagina
itching or irritation around the vagina
risk_factors_triggers: Vaginal cleansing and douching can increase the risk of developing BV. Intravaginal practice, e.g. insertion of herbs or other products into the vagina, is another risk factor.
who_response: Women who present with vaginal discharge, and who are managed based on the syndromic approach are treated for BV, candidiasis and trichomoniasis. Metronidazole is indicated for both BV and trichomonas, while topical or oral antifungals are indicated for candidiasis.
